clue.text: Killing like Eagle, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: killing in the informal sense of hilariously funny
the Eagle was a British children's comic paper, so something like it is comic-like

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses lead to funny: a killing joke is hilarious, and anything like a comic paper is comic in style.

clue.text: A good deal of a wag at Wimbledon?

definitions.meaning: a valuable picture card, a king, queen or jack, received when cards are dealt
a card is a joker or wag, and Wimbledon's tennis is played on a court

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, played on courts; a card is a wag or comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A king, queen or jack is a valuable card in a deal, and a card is also a joker.

clue.text: Satisfied with carriers, in some ways

parts.note: met as in met the requirements
hods are builders' carriers for bricks

explanation.surface: Content with the porters, in certain respects.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is a trough on a pole for carrying bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Methods are procedures, means of doing something.

clue.text: Saw employer hold eminent artist up in middle of New York

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: center is the American spelling of middle, as written in New York

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: PRA is the President of the Royal Academy, a leading artist

explanation.surface: A man with a saw keeps a great painter in mid-Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PRA to ARP and 'hold' puts it in CENTER. 'Saw' looks like a verb, but is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker is someone who uses a saw for his craft.

clue.text: Beat beginner first, then expert

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, so a beginner
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Defeat a novice first and then a master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first, then' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace someone is to thrash or beat them.

clue.text: Boldness of desperado pocketing a coin once

indicators.note: the desperado puts the other pieces in his pocket, so they go inside

parts.note: a bravo is a hired ruffian or desperado
D stood for the old British penny (denarius) before decimalisation

explanation.surface: A bold outlaw keeps an antique coin in his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts A and D inside BRAVO. D is the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of daring, a swaggering kind of boldness.

clue.text: B--- awful weather brings sudden inspiration

parts.note: the printed letter with dashes stands for a mild oath, giving the letter B
a rainstorm is foul weather

explanation.surface: Bloody awful weather sparks a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The page has no 'I'; 'B---' is a censored oath, giving its letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden clever idea or flash of thought.

clue.text: Distribute complete set of books

parts.note: all means whole or complete
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Share out an entire collection of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or apportion.

clue.text: A notion to revise part of Shakespeare

indicators.note: revising alters the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idea to rework a Shakespeare role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to revise' rearranges A NOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A role in The Merchant of Venice and other plays by the Bard.

clue.text: Honours English with 24

definitions.note: the cross-reference to the solution at 24 Across, a pot belly, makes this an adjective

parts.note: OBEs are British honours (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: Honours list for Englishmen with big bellies.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to 24 Across, a belly, so having one means being fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a big belly is the mark of someone very fat.

clue.text: Headless golf-club, say

indicators.note: the club loses its head, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A golf club has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' removes the first letter P from PUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak or voice it.

clue.text: Hot claret might make her drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A glass of mulled red wine might get a woman tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals a rearrangement of HOT CLARET; 'her' is the whole definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a woman's name, so a female person referred to as her.

clue.text: Moreover, was first to be decorated

parts.note: too means also or moreover
led means was in front, first in a race

explanation.surface: Someone besides was also the first to receive an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooled leather is decorated with impressed designs worked by a hot tool.

clue.text: Full of wise saws and modern ---s" (AYLI)

definitions.text: Full of wise saws and modern ---s

parts.words: Full of wise saws and modern ---s
parts.note: a gap-fill from Jaques's Seven Ages of Man speech in As You Like It (AYLI), describing the justice

explanation.walkthrough: AYLI is As You Like It; the justice in the speech is full of proverbs and up-to-date examples.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quotation means examples or cases, hence modern examples alongside old sayings.

clue.text: Role for Casanova in Othello?

parts.note: a seducer's role, but Othello literally kills a woman, Desdemona

explanation.definitionFit: The term for a seducer of women is also literal for Othello, who murders his wife.

clue.text: Advantage, some say, since firm amalgamated

indicators.note: the two pieces are merged into a single word

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
set means firm or solid, like set jelly

explanation.surface: Some claim a merger brought a company benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' is a link: the word is a colloquial name for any advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that gives an advantage.

clue.text: Opposed to strike demand of some drivers

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
knock means hit or strike

explanation.surface: Drivers oppose a strike call.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists once wanted petrol with an additive that stops engine pinking, a property they demanded of fuel.

clue.text: Carried away by a novel

definitions.meaning: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure story of 1886

explanation.definitionFit: Abducted describes someone carried off; it is also the title of Stevenson's tale of David Balfour.

clue.text: Military commander lost in Hampshire

parts.note: the Field Marshal drowned in 1916 when the cruiser HMS Hampshire sank, not in the English county

explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire looks like the southern English county; it is a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: The British war minister died aboard the cruiser HMS Hampshire when it hit a mine off Orkney.

clue.text: Orders yet another sort of ship

indicators.note: the words are recast into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Commands for still one more kind of vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another sort of' rearranges ORDERS YET; the definition is just 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval warship.

clue.text: Can't break into money for study

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the money word

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

indicators.note: breaking the word scatters its letters

explanation.surface: Unable to dip into savings for a home office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' here is a room, not reading; 'break' scrambles the contraction and 'into' sends it inside the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room or den, a quiet place to work.

clue.text: Fleet Street supremo returned to station

indicators.note: returned means coming back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a newspaper's top man is the top ed (editor); Fleet Street was the home of London's national press

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief went back to the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses TOP ED. Fleet Street is the London street long home to British newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a station or base, for buses, trains or supplies.

clue.text: Quaker worker displays flag

parts.note: William Penn, Quaker founder of Pennsylvania
the worker ant is crossword shorthand for a worker

explanation.surface: A Quaker labourer shows a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennant is a long tapering flag, as on ships.

clue.text: Type of transport for flier on moon trip

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another comes after it
a trip is a stumble, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: a rail is a marsh bird, so a flier

explanation.surface: A suggested vehicle to carry an airman to the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' looks like an airman, but it is the marsh bird; 'trip' scrambles the moon and 'on' places the bird after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A monorail is a railway running on a single track, a mode of transport.

clue.text: Numbers of Romans copy so precisely

definitions.meaning: M, I, M, I and C are all Roman numerals

explanation.definitionFit: The word is spelt entirely in Roman numerals and means to imitate closely.

clue.text: Set some free — verdict of magistrate

indicators.note: only some of the letters are set out, a run spanning the words

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling releases several defendants.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'fREE VErdict'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or magistrate in medieval England.

clue.text: A strike-breaker in the corporation

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the strike word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to punch is to strike

explanation.surface: A scab working within a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is old slang for a large belly, not a company; 'breaker' puts A into PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a jocular old word for a fat stomach, a pot belly.

clue.text: Girl produces a duplicate without names

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the pair goes round
duplicate means two copies of the single letter

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two Ns for names

explanation.surface: A girl makes a copy of something without naming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicate' doubles A, and 'without' (outside) puts the pair round NN.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, a female given name.

clue.text: Left eight men brewing mead

indicators.note: brewing stirs the letters together into a new mixture

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eight men who remained are making a honey drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges L plus EIGHT MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Metheglin is a spiced Welsh variety of mead, the fermented honey drink.

clue.text: Clear, even in speech

indicators.note: spoken, the word for level sounds the same as the answer

parts.note: a plane surface is flat and even

explanation.surface: Something is obvious, even when said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says the word for even (PLANE) sounds like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means obvious or easy to understand.

clue.text: In firm, many look equal

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, hence many
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Inside the company, lots of people appear the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is a peer or companion of equal standing.

clue.text: Financial investigator said abroad to be surrounded by gold

indicators.note: the gold pieces stand either side of the other piece

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
or is gold in heraldry
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: An accountant spoke overseas while wrapped in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'gold' serves twice, as the chemical symbol and the heraldic tincture; 'surrounded by' wraps them round the French word for said.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects a company's accounts, investigating its finances.
